#392 fix r3.summary: #392 round 3 is in /tmp/wt-392 as one commit, c72ec3a0. It sits on main 61f03b67, the rebase had no conflicts, and nothing was pushed. Every blocking item was reproduced on the round-2 code before it was fixed. (1) A relative path in an installer variable is now refused (exit 2) for a catalog install and for update, and the message names the variable. The variables are UV_CONFIG_FILE, UV_INDEX_URL, UV_DEFAULT_INDEX, UV_INDEX, UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL, UV_FIND_LINKS, the uv constraint and override files, SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CLIENT_CERT, and the PIP_* config, index, find-links, constraint, requirement and cert values. Before the fix, uv read aelix's empty uv.toml and dropped missing local indexes without an error; pip ignored relative find-links and index values with only a warning, and a relative PIP_CONFIG_FILE silently. The model now joins a relative UV_CONFIG_FILE to the child's cwd. The pip.conf translation was off for a different reason than round 2 said: any UV_CONFIG_FILE value turns it off (the _UV_INDEX_ENV rule). (2) catalog_installer_cwd checks with lstat. A link (a symlink, or a junction on Windows) or the wrong kind of entry, for the directory or for either sentinel, is refused. A sentinel link is refused even when its target holds the exact sentinel text. On POSIX the work runs through an O_NOFOLLOW directory handle and files are created O_EXCL; on Windows it is lstat followed by O_EXCL, and that check-then-use race is written down as a limit. (3) PipRunner is now a protocol with a cwd keyword. Every runner, default or injected, is called as runner(argv, cwd=installer-cwd), including for the verify download. A runner that takes no cwd is refused for catalog installs and updates, and still drives a typed install. (4) The consent line now reads 'the installer runs in DIR'. (5) Any value with an RFC 3986 scheme is treated as a URL, so file:/ is never anchored; C:/x stays a path. (6) Seven model layouts were added (nineteen in total). The model was wrong for a [project] with an invalid name, and that is fixed. There are now rows for the system index and for an empty XDG_CONFIG_DIRS entry (uv 0.12 behaviour; 0.11 differs, recorded in the ADR). ADR-0255 section 15, ADR-0200 section 12, the decisions index, the guide and its bundled copy, and the CHANGELOG are updated.

findings.title: 1a. Relative UV_CONFIG_FILE with a scheme-like name bypasses the refusal
findings.detail: The relative-path guard accepts URL-scheme-looking values, but uv reads UV_CONFIG_FILE as a filesystem path. UV_CONFIG_FILE=file:pin.toml is a relative POSIX filename. uv resolves it against installer-cwd, not the user's cwd, and the refusal never fires. This happens for both discover install and update.
findings.evidence: Script .omc/probes/392-live/r3cross/scripts/relative_config_scheme.py, run with 'uv run --no-sync python'. Output: 'IS_ABSOLUTE=False', 'RELATIVE_GUARD=[]', discover install 'rc=0 ORIGIN=INSTALLER-CONFIG-DECOY', update 'rc=0 ORIGIN=INSTALLER-CONFIG-DECOY'. Reproduced on uv 0.11.19 and 0.12.23.

findings.title: 1b. Python API install_extension(resolve_entry_target(entry)) still runs in the caller cwd
findings.detail: install_extension defaults to neutral_cwd=False, even when it gets the ResolvedPath that the catalog resolver returns. Through the Python API, the uv.toml in the caller's cwd (find-links ./w) supplies a decoy dependency. The CLI catalog route sets the flag correctly.

findings.detail: The refusal message says 'Set UV_CONFIG_FILE to an absolute path (or a URL)', and docs/guides/private-catalog.md:306 says the same. uv treats the value as a path, so a file:// URL fails even when the file exists.
